elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to an affiliate
elements.evidence: The Company may assign this Agreement without HDI's consent to an affiliate

elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to a successor in merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets
elements.evidence: or to a successor in a merger, an acquisition or a sale of substantially all assets

elements.element: Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent
elements.evidence: HDI may not assign this Agreement without the Company's prior written consent

elements.element: Customer's consent not to be unreasonably withheld
elements.evidence: such consent not to be unreasonably withheld

elements.element: Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor
elements.evidence: and in no event to a competitor of the Company

elements.element: No Vendor termination right on Customer's change of control
elements.evidence: HDI shall have no right to terminate this Agreement as a result of a change of control of the Company

elements.element: Mutual right to assign to successors with written notice
elements.evidence: Vendor-side assignment requires consent, and no written-notice mechanic appears: "HDI may not assign this Agreement without the Company's prior written consent"

elements.element: Consent for other assignments not unreasonably withheld
elements.evidence: such consent not to be unreasonably withheld

reasons: The inserted sentences supply every atomic element of the preferred position: Customer affiliate and M&A successor assignment without consent, Vendor assignment only with Customer's prior written consent (not unreasonably withheld), an absolute competitor bar, and no Vendor termination right on Customer change of control.
Fallback is not independently satisfied (no mutual successor-assignment-on-notice right for Vendor), but that is immaterial since the locked preferred level is fully met.
Minimal: a concise insertion after the untouched binding-effect sentence, which previously did not regulate assignment at all; no rewrite, no new exceptions, no boilerplate.
Intent preserved: original successors-and-assigns language remains effective, defined terms Company and HDI are used correctly, and no dangling mechanic or contradiction is introduced.
